Title: Regression: [Snappi] Tests using dynamic port selection logic are getting skipped incorrectly

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Previous Working Version

202411

### Steps to Reproduce

Run tests from `tests/snappi_tests` using `tgen_port_info` fixture (you'll see that these tests are getting skipped)

### Impact of this regression

Test cases won't be running as they were getting skipped incorrectly.

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/15069 has introduced dynamic port selection which is achieved by fixture tgen_port_info.

With above change all the test cases using tgen_port_info are getting skipped incorrectly with signature got empty parameter set ['tgen_port_info'], function ...

More details:
tgen_port_info fixture (see [get_snappi_testbed_metadata](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/202505/tests/conftest.py#L1493-L1513)) depends on metadata tests/metadata/snappi_tests which is supposed to be populated by pretest [test_update_snappi_testbed_metadata](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/202505/tests/test_pretest.py#L216)

But this pretest is getting skipped due to check pytest_require(("tgen" in (request.config.getoption("--topology") or "")) see https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/202505/tests/test_pretest.py#L220-L221, this check expects "tgen" in topology which makes sense for snappi topologies (as we pass tgen or multidut-tgen to the run_tests.sh -t argument). But for pretests pytest will be called with --topology util (see [UTIL_TOPOLOGY_OPTIONS](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/202505/tests/run_tests.sh#L306)) instead of TEST_TOPOLOGY_OPTIONS thus causing above pretest to get skipped along with snappi testcases using tgen_port_info fixture.

Title: Bug: packets in ACL tests being dropped or using wrong route after reboot / port toggle due to higher convergence time needed when large amount of routes

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

On dT2 during ACL tests, after reboot or port toggle resets the BGP connections, if a test tries to verify a packets expected route through the dT2 too soon after the toggle, the device may send it through the wrong route or drop the packet. We see that for some T2 we need this change as well, we suspect this is due to a high number of routes

### Steps to Reproduce

Mimic the ACL test on a device with many routes advertised to it (T2/dT2 typically): send a packet with a destination IP with an expected downlink route through uplink shortly after BGP comes up, after port toggle or reboot.

We see it rarely when running the ACL test (hard/time-consuming to reproduce individually, but running the whole suite tends to get at least 1 or 2 errors), resulting in errors such as: `Did not receive expected packet on any of ports [...]` and `Received expected packet on port X for device 0, but it should have arrived on one of these ports: [...]`

The route the packet takes should be as expected

Title: [Snappi]: PFC m2o lossy test has lossy priorities hardcoded to 0 and 1.

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

The m2o lossy case:
- Test has 2 ingress interfaces and 1 egress interface.
- Ingress interfaces has test flow of lossy priority of 30% and background lossless priority flow of 25%.
- Cumulative ingress traffic is 60% lossy traffic and 50% lossless traffic.

In test script should randomize the priorities in the lossy priorities between [0, 1, 2, 5, 6]. However, helper file eventually chooses priority 0 and 1 ONLY, thus limiting the testcase.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure(hardcode) the lossy priority to 5 and 6 in the test-script:
```
test_prio_list = [5, 6]
```
2. Run the test-case and check for the queue-counters. The queue counters will ONLY show priority 0 and 1.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The test-script has following code to select the lossy priorities:
```
test_prio_list = [x for x in all_prio_list if x not in pause_prio_list]
```

The helper file has following code:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/09d1c4d927d19a3eafc82de065d37a90a2ba9b7d/tests/snappi_tests/pfc/files/m2o_oversubscribe_lossy_helper.py#L112C1-L127C58

```
    __gen_traffic(testbed_config=testbed_config,
                  port_config_list=port_config_list,

                  tx_port_id_list=tx_port_id_list,
                  pause_flow_name=PAUSE_FLOW_NAME,
                  pause_prio_list=pause_prio_list,
                  test_flow_name=TEST_FLOW_NAME,

                  data_pkt_size=DATA_PKT_SIZE,
                  prio_dscp_map=prio_dscp_map,
                  no_of_lossy_streams=no_of_test_streams)
```

This is further called to generate test_flows:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/09d1c4d927d19a3eafc82de065d37a90a2ba9b7d/tests/snappi_tests/pfc/files/m2o_oversubscribe_lossy_helper.py#L231C1-L241C56
```
    __gen_data_flows(testbed_config=testbed_config,
                     port_config_list=port_config_list,

                     flow_prio_list=test_flow_prio_list,

```

This in turn calls following code:

```
    if pfcQueueGroupSize == 8:

    elif 'Test Flow 1 -> 0' in flow.name:

Bug: Missing admin_status in CONFIG_DB for interfaces not part of sonic-mgmt topology
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

When deploying the minigraph using sonic-mgmt scripts, the minigraph command sets the "admin_status" to "up" only for interfaces that are part of the defined topology. Interfaces not included in the topology are left without an "admin_status" field in the configuration.

This omission causes components like buffermgrd to indefinitely wait for the "admin_status" field. During test execution, if sonic-mgmt test cases attempt to shut down interfaces that are not part of the topology, the "admin_status" for those interfaces is then added to CONFIG_DB. As a result, buffermgrd, which had been waiting for this field, immediately applies buffer profile updates to the interface. This unexpected behavior can lead to test case failures, particularly those involving checkpoint validations.

        "path": "/PORT/Ethernet0/admin_status",
        "value": "down"

]
```
3. apply patch

config apply-patch eth_admin_patch.json

Title: Bug: BUFFER_PG profile configs are not applied correctly for lossless queues 3-4 after port breakout

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

For lossless queues, the BUFFER_PG profile is expected to be auto-generated by buffermgrd based on the port’s speed and cable length. This profile is applied to the lossless queues accordingly.

However, during port breakout, BUFFER_PG settings are applied only to the primary (first) port. The remaining breakout ports receive only the default configuration for lossless queues.

This behavior is due to buffermgrd relying on the port’s admin_status in CONFIG_DB to trigger BUFFER_PG application. Since the newly created breakout ports lack admin_status entries in CONFIG_DB, the configuration is deferred until the port’s admin_status is manually toggled to "up" or "down".

Adding admin_status entries for each port in /etc/sonic/port_breakout_config_db.json is cumbersome.
A more streamlined approach is preferred to ensure consistent BUFFER_PG configuration for lossless queues across all breakout ports.

### Description of PR
test_crm_nexthop_group was failing on sn4700 testbeds due to a known orchagent crash. The crash is caused by a few factors:

- Expected neighbor entry missing from kernel, causing tunnel-route to be programmed for unresolved nexthop.
- tunnel-route being removed when nexthop group was deleted
- route bulker ending early due to ITEM_NOT_FOUND (not processing remaining bulk removes)
- next-hop group delete failing due to OBJECT_IN_USE.

This PR addresses the first issue.

During neighbor generation for the test, some of the neighbor updates were being missed from APPL_DB on sn4700 devices. Previously, the neighbors were programmed in the kernel in a single ip command, this fix splits up the neighbor programming into batches in order to prevent updates from being dropped.

Title: Bug: 'config route add' incorrectly adds an empty string for default vrf

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

After adding a static route, `config reload` fails with a YANG validation error.

```
sudo config route add prefix <IP>/16 nexthop <IP>
```
generates the following in ConfigDB:
```
"STATIC_ROUTE": {
    "default|<IP>/16": {
        "blackhole": "false",
        "distance": "0",
        "ifname": "",
        "nexthop": "<IP>",
        "nexthop-vrf": ""
    }
},
```

We have "" passed as an entry for nexthop-vrf in our default config_db.json. Subsequent calls to `config replace` fail due to this entry.

```
admin@tb3-dut:~$ sudo config replace /etc/sonic/config_db.json
Config Replacer: Config replacement starting.
Config Replacer: Target config length: 36417.
Config Replacer: Getting current config db.
Config Replacer: Generating patch between target config and current config db.
Config Replacer: Applying patch using 'Patch Applier'.
Patch Applier: localhost: Patch application starting.
Patch Applier: localhost: Patch: []
Patch Applier: localhost getting current config db.
Patch Applier: localhost: simulating the target full config after applying the patch.
Patch Applier: localhost: validating all JsonPatch operations are permitted on the specified fields
Patch Applier: localhost: validating target config does not have empty tables,
                            since they do not show up in ConfigDb.
Patch Applier: localhost: sorting patch updates.
Failed to replace config
Usage: config replace [OPTIONS] TARGET_FILE_PATH
Try "config replace -h" for help.

Error: Given patch will produce invalid config. Error: Data Loading Failed
Value "" does not satisfy the constraint "(((Vrf[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)|(default)|(mgmt)),)*((Vrf[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)|(default)|(mgmt))" (range, length, or pattern).
```

We can see from https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/47687229f3a3cde08e9d144c1668c44a04dee41c/src/sonic-yang-models/yang-models/sonic-static-route.yang#L114 that the empty string is not a valid vrf identifier for a nexthop-vrf:
```
        leaf nexthop-vrf {
          type string {
            pattern "((((Vrf[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)|(default)|(mgmt)),)*((Vrf[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)|(default)|(mgmt)))?";
          }
          description
            "VRF name of the nexthop. This is for vrf leaking";
        }
```

This can either be fixed by adding the string 'default' instead of '' for nexthops in the default vrf, or by adding '' to the YANG definition.

sudo config route add prefix <IP>/16 nexthop <IP>
sudo config reload

`config reload` fails after running `config prefix add`

`config reload` should pass after running `config prefix add`

#### What I did

The config route commands accept a `nexthop-vrf` as an argument. When that argument is not specified, the commands use the empty string as the default. This violates the yang model, which only accepts vrf names of the form (`default`, `mgmt`, or `Vrf*`). In the case where a `nexthop-vrf` is not defined, we should fall back to using the same vrf given for the prefix we are adding. If that is not specified, then both prefix and nexthop will use the default vrf.

Fixes: [#22420](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/22420)

#### How I did it

Modify the` add_route()` and `del_route()` codepaths from sonic-utilites/config/main.py to set nexthop-vrf to whatever the vrf is for the associated prefix whenever it is not explicitly specified.

#### How to verify it

All unit tests pass (including all tests in `static_route_test.py`).

I don't think the output of any show commands changes because of this, but it's possible there are combinations of different VRFs which would show up differently. Before this merges I'll set up some routes and nexthops with different VRFs and make sure any changes there may be are shown here.

Title: Bug: [SmartSwitch] IP will not be assigned on midplane after DPU Image Upgrade from 202505 -> 202506+

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

DHCP Server on NPU is not assigning Ip to DPU after upgrade from 202505 -> 202506+

### Steps to Reproduce

1) Install Image on NPU, setup smartswitch config and start dhcp_server
2) Install 202505 on DPU / or power on DPU which has 202505 by default
3) NPU assigns IP to DPU
4) Install 202506 image.
5) Check if IP is not assigned and is accessible from NPU

IP will not be assigned to DPU. IP will be assigned after 3600 sec (This is lease expiration time) from the time of Step #3.  This is often too late and service will be started with incorrent database config and can lead to crash in DPU

Happening because of this change where the Client-ID in the DHCP request is different between 202505/202506

Bug: [SmartSwitch] IP will not be assigned on midplane after DPU Image Upgrade from 202505 -> 202506+
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

DHCP Server on NPU is not assigning Ip to DPU after upgrade from 202505 -> 202506+

### Steps to Reproduce

1) Install Image on NPU, setup smartswitch config and start dhcp_server
2) Install 202505 on DPU / or power on DPU which has 202505 by default
3) NPU assigns IP to DPU
4) Install 202506 image.
5) Check if IP is not assigned and is accessible from NPU

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

IP will not be assigned to DPU. IP will be assigned after 3600 sec (This is lease expiration time) from the time of Step #3.  This is often too late and service will be started with incorrent database config and can lead to crash in DPU

### Triage
Happening because of this change where the Client-ID in the DHCP request is different between 202505/202506

Change was made here: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/23805

And the dhcp_server thinks the request is coming from a new device and it doesn't allocate the IP until the original lease expires

Where the ClientIdentifier was explicitly set to mac

Title: Enhancement: [sflow] Enable test_sflow.py for 'vs' topologies

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the enhancement

Currently, `sflow/test_sflow.py` is disabled for virtual topologies, and is being skipped for those topos. This is unfortunate, because the community test suite relies on virtual testbeds to test against when changes are made to sonic-mgmt. This means that changes made to `sflow/test_sflow.py` are not validated against the community test infrastructure, which creates a test gap as we do not do any verification of those changes (the test is skipped and marked as PASSED without ever running any testcases).

I ran the test against a virtual topology and it seems to pass just fine. I'm not sure what the original logic was, as the skip has been moved around through several files and I can't find the first reference, but I think if the test passes on the topo then it should be safe to remove the skip.

If we want the test to run on the community infra, however, we'll need to add logic to enable sflow for that test explicitly. This could be done at the infrastructure level by passing `--enable_sflow_feature` to the test when it's run as part of the CI/CD pipeline, although since I don't have access to that process I'm not sure how possible that is. The alternative is to _always_ enable the feature when the test is run on a virtual topology. That's probably not a bad approach, since we generally assume that the whole point of having a virtual topology is to run this explicit test (whereas a physical testbed may be set to test non-standard configuration or network structure).

### Current Behavior

The test is skipped for VS topos.

### Proposed Behavior

The test runs on VS topos.

Title: Bug: [ztp] ZTP cannot find IP6 default routes on eth0

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

Currently, all interfaces in a sonic device are set to be IPv6 forwarding interfaces. This causes an issue because they won't honor RA advertisements. Also, currently, the IPv6 `dhclient` gets a prefix allocation, so by default, the interface receives a /128 address from the DHCPv6 server with no default route. The default behavior of ZTP is to try to find a DHCP server using the default route, if it exists. If there is no IPv6 default route, ZTP will fail unless some alternative is provided.

To address this, `eth0` can be set to host mode in the ZTP config script, so that it will accept RA, perform SLAAC, and retrieve the remaining information from the DHCPv6 server.

* The dash-api package is reverted to install from source code. The dash-api debian package built in bookworm cannot be installed in Ubuntu 24.04 due to dependency issues.
* Default user "ubuntu" of Ubuntu 24.04 is removed from the image to avoid potential issues. For details, please refer to https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/20761. * Improved the code for installing docker and azure-cli.

Title: Test Gap: Warm-booted state matches cold boot state

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the test gap

In SONiC, the expectation is that the state of a device warm-upgraded into a version matches the state of that same device cold-booting into the same version. When these don't match, unexpected things can happen during device operation.

### Affected Area

Warm Reboot

### Impact of missing tests and proposed tests

There should be a test that snapshots the system (CONFIG, APPL, ASIC, STATE, etc DB's) after warm-upgrade then does a cold reboot, takes another snapshot and compares the two. Any mis-match will cause an error.

Retrieved SONiC documentation:

[1] warm-reboot/Multi_ASIC_warm_reboot.md — Ignoring failing ASICs (score=132.613)
Some ASICs may be in a bad unrecoverable state. In this case the user should be able to warm-reboot healthy ASICs while the failing ASIC should be cold started.

The `warm-reboot` is extended with option `-m` (*mask asic*) that accepts a comma seperated list of ASICs to skip warm-boot process on. 
Instead these ASICs are going to be cold booted at startup.


**Affected components**:
  - sonic-utilities scripts:
    - warm-reboot
    - check_db_integrity
    - lag_keepalive
    - sonic-db-dump
    - centralize_database
    - teamd_increase_retry_count

[2] warm-reboot/Multi_ASIC_warm_reboot.md — Warm shutdown (score=119.254)
Entrypoint for warmboot is `warm-reboot` command.

`warm-reboot` script updates:

- Single ASIC shutdown sequence remains exactly the same
- Shutdown sequence from the perspective of a single ASIC in a Multi ASIC environment remains the same
- On a Mutli-ASIC device the `warm-reboot` script maintains a list of ASICs to operate on
- Every ASIC specific operation is executed for each ASIC in parallel:
  - e.g: ```docker exec -it swss$dev orchagent_restart_check``` 
- In case of ASIC failure (e.g: restart_check failure), that ASIC is removed from the list, ASIC is cold booted in startup path

[3] bmc/graceful-shutdown/switch-host-graceful-shutdown-hld.md — 10. Warmboot and Fastboot Design Impact (score=117.665)
This is a shutdown path. It is never on the warm-boot or fast-boot code path and changes neither.

One interaction is deliberate: like any `reboot`, a graceful shutdown clears staged warm-boot state,
because the host will be cold-booted after power is removed. A staged warm reboot and a BMC graceful
shutdown are opposite intents, and the operator sequences them.

### Description of PR

Summary:
Fixes #18970
MSFT ADO: 33268881

This PR introduces a new T0 test called `test_warmboot_data_consistency` which:
    1. Installs the base image and boots into clean state
    2. Installs target image
    3. Performs warm reboot and take database snapshots
    4. Performs cold reboot and take database snapshots
    5. Compares snapshots and analyze differences
    6. Prune expected differences (e.g. volatile values) and report unexpected ones

Currently only comparison between CONFIG, APPL and STATE DB's of cold and warm boots is supported. Any differences are logged out on the console and do not fail the test. There is a separate work item here (#21226 ) to add this support.

Test **artifacts** include:
- sairedis/swss/syslog after base, warm and cold boot
- APPL, STATE, CONFIG, ASIC DB dumps after warm and cold boot
- Processed result of the difference between the cold vs warm of each of the DB. There are two variants:
  - Pre-Prune (e.g. `appl_diff_prune.json`) - this is the comparison result of the raw unprocessed DB dumps
  - Post-Prune (e.g. `appl_diff_post_prune.json`) - this is the comparison result of the DB's with the volatile keys such as cpu, temperature, timestamps, etc filtered out.

Here's a snippet of an inconsistency reported in a `state_diff_post_prune.json` output:
```
"TUNNEL_DECAP_TABLE|IPINIP_TUNNEL": {
            "value": {
                "dscp_mode": {
                    "after_warmboot": "uniform",
                    "after_coldboot": "pipe"
                },
                "ecn_mode": {
                    "after_warmboot": "standard",
                    "after_coldboot": "copy_from_outer"
                }
            }
        },
```

Additionally, **metrics** are pushed into the custom msg utility of the test result which is available in the test result XML file (`test_warmboot_data_consistency.py::test_warmboot_data_consistency.xml`). Definitions, for these metrics are found in `tests/common/db_comparison.py::DbComparison`. It is recommended to ingest these metrics to track the downtrend over time as these inconsistencies are fixed (utilities in test_reporting/ can help with this).

#### What I did
Fixed `show ip route <protocol> json` commands producing invalid JSON output with namespace prefix.

Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/24398
Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/issues/3687

#### How I did it

The root cause is `show/bgp_common.py` have a special if clause for protocol filters (bgp, static, etc.), triggering namespace-prefix output path even when JSON is requested.

[Current logic:](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/blob/3994fcdee03cd6f8752f8b22e541ba13c778dc2c/show/bgp_common.py#L405-L409)
```python3
if found_other_parms:
    print("{}:".format(ns))   # Prints ': ' on single-ASIC (ns='')
    print(output)
    continue                  # Skips JSON processing
```

[Solution:](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/blob/e8debf2cd9d2b53b74303d621303b0c3d57fb312/show/bgp_common.py#L405-L409)

```python3
if found_other_parms and not found_json:
    print("{}:".format(ns))
    print(output)
    continue
```

We simply skip namespace-prefix path when JSON output is requested.
This allows JSON requests to fall through to [proper JSON processing later at line 413](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/blob/3994fcdee03cd6f8752f8b22e541ba13c778dc2c/show/bgp_common.py#L432-L433).

Test protocol-filtered route commands with JSON output:
```
show ip route bgp json
show ip route static json
show ip route connected json
```

Verify output starts with `{` and is valid JSON (parseable with `jq` or `python -m json.tool`).

Verify non-JSON commands still work:
```
show ip route bgp
show ip route
```

#### Description

Remove calls to setting a syslog tag as there was no logging actually used in this module. The existing call to log a message was in dead code, therefore there was no need to setup a syslogger at all.

#### Motivation and Context

In python services using `sonic_py_common.logger` the syslog identifier already set up by the executable/service can be overwritten when importing other modules.

This log hijack is coming from a library: `sonic_platform_base/sonic_xcvr/api/public/c_cmis.py`
```
SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER = "CCmisApi"
...
helper_logger = logger.Logger(SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER)
# This is the only log that this file has:
    helper_logger.log_debug('key {} not present in VDM'.format(new_key))
```

Searching in the syslog of a switch running SONiC we see logs with the `CCmisApi` that shouldn't:
```
2025-11-11T13:20:03.440479+00:00 sonic CCmisApi: Failed to load platform Pcie module. Warning : No module named 'sonic_platform.pcie', fallback to load Pcie common utility.
2025 Nov 11 <IPV6>.179454 gold228 NOTICE CCmisApi: System is ready
```

If any code imports c_cmis.py (indirectly for the most part) and has a logger session open already, their existing session will be re-opened with a new log tag, `CCmisApi` which is not desired.

To fix this we remove this logging code entirely because the function where it is used became dead in #556

Libraries (rather than executables) probably shouldn't be syslogging on their own, and they certainly shouldn't hijack the log tag of the including executable.

Resolves sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#24489

#### How Has This Been Tested?

Before the fix:
Open an interactive python session and run this code:
```
from sonic_py_common import logger
log = logger.Logger("NATE")
log.log_notice("Log 1")
import sonic_platform
log.log_notice("Log 2")
```
Watch the syslog output:
```
2025 Nov 11 <IPV6>.002667 gold228-dut NOTICE NATE: Log 1
2025 Nov 11 <IPV6>.406481 gold228-dut NOTICE CCmisApi: Log 2
```
Clearly the second log should also have had the tag `NATE`

After the fix:
Syslog entries should have been:
```
2025 Nov 11 <IPV6>.002667 gold228-dut NOTICE NATE: Log 1
2025 Nov 11 <IPV6>.406481 gold228-dut NOTICE NATE: Log 2
```

Title: Test Gap: Add a test to verify correctness of PSU Status

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the test gap

A test gap exists in the current PSU status verification logic, specifically within `test_get_status` (or related test suites that check PSU health). The current tests only assert that a boolean value (True or False) is returned by the getStatus method, but they do not confirm that the status is set to True when all underlying metrics (current, voltage, power) are within acceptable operational bounds.

This prevents us from detecting regressions where the PSU hardware is healthy, but the software logic fails to correctly translate the nominal state into a Power Good signal.

### Affected Area

PSU Health (Applicable to all platforms)

### Impact of missing tests and proposed tests

We will miss scenarios where the PSU status is incorrectly reported by the software when the underlying hardware is healthy.

Retrieved SONiC documentation:

[1] psud/PSU_daemon_design.md — 1. Overview (score=177.667)
The purpose of PSU daemon is to collect platform PSU data and trigger proper actions if necessary. Major functions of psud include:

- Collect constant PSU data during daemon boot up, such as PSU number.
- Collect variable PSU data periodically, including:
  - PSU entity information
  - PSU present status and power good status
  - PSU power, current, voltage and voltage threshold

### Description of PR

The test uses the `docker exec pmon find /` command, which can exit with rc=1 due to transient `/proc` entries disappearing during the search — even when `y_cable_simulated.py` is found and printed to stdout.
This causes `RunAnsibleModuleFail` before the path is assigned, leading to `UnboundLocalError: local variable 'y_cable_simulated_path' referenced before assignment` in the `finally` block during cleanup.

**Fix**:
- Suppress stderr warnings with `2>/dev/null`
- Ignore non-zero exit codes via `module_ignore_errors=True` to make the lookup reliable

#### What is the motivation for this PR?

This change eliminates a flaky failure in `test_switchover_faulty_ycable.py` observed on dual-TOR testbeds.
The failure is intermittent (~10–30% rate depending on system load) because the `find /` command traverses `/` and encounters transient `/proc/<pid>` directories that disappear mid-execution. This causes `find` to exit with rc=1 even when the target file path is correctly printed to stdout.
The test code does not tolerate this non-zero return code → `RunAnsibleModuleFail` is raised before path assignment → `UnboundLocalError` during teardown/cleanup.

#### How did you do it?

- Added `2>/dev/null` to the `find` command to suppress the noisy `/proc/... No such file or directory` warnings on stderr
- Added `module_ignore_errors=True` to the `duthost.shell()` call so that a non-zero return code does not raise `RunAnsibleModuleFail` when stdout still contains the expected path

#### How did you verify/test it?

- Ran test_switchover_faulty_ycable.py  in a loop (20+ consecutive runs) on a  dual-TOR testbed
- Verified in test logs that `/proc` warnings no longer appear and cleanup executes cleanly without exceptions

#### Any platform specific information?

Primarily reproducible on multi-ASIC SONiC platforms using the `pmon` container

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A (robustness improvement to existing dual-TOR test)

N/A – no new feature or new test case. This is a targeted fix for test reliability.

### Description of PR

Summary:
Remove `test_gnmi_configdb_full_01` which incorrectly used `gnoi_reboot` as a config reload mechanism. The test was pushing config via GNMI, then calling `gnoi_reboot` expecting the config to be applied after reboot - this conflates reboot with config reload, which are fundamentally different operations.

Fixes #17436

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

The test `test_gnmi_configdb_full_01` was using `gnoi_reboot` incorrectly - treating it as a config reload mechanism rather than an actual device reboot. This represents a flawed test design that tests incorrect behavior.

#### How did you do it?

However, as part of the setup for this test, `ConfigFileContext(duthost, os.path.join(FILES_DIR, IGNORE_DEVICE_CHECK_CONFIG_FILE))` has been invoked which puts https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/system_health/files/ignore_device_check.json in place of the system's default health checker config. This contains:
```
    "led_color": {
      "fault": "orange",
```

This creates 2 possibilties for how this test can go:
1. If the device doesn't support "orange" as a system LED color, it will fail to set the color and fail the test because the LED is still green/healthy. We see this in the test above, note the `Invalid color` log before the normal output in `system_health_summary`.
2. If the device does support "orange", the device will set its system led to orange/fault and the test will fail because the color isn't in the checked set, yellow, amber, and red.

Reviewing the test, I'm not sure it's possible to pass as is.

We can fix this for case 1 above by omitting the `ConfigFileContext` for this test, I'm not sure it is required for this test. I'll send a PR with this fix.

For number 2, we could add orange to the list of "bad" colors in check_system_health_led_info.

However, I think there is a more fundamental problem with the test_system_health.py tests overriding the system health checker config with colors that the devices don't support. I'm not sure what the best way to solve that is.

## Description

Fixes healthd/sysmonitor crashing with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` when receiving dbus events for systemd units whose names contain multiple dots.

**Root cause:** `event.split(".")` in both `get_unit_status()` and `check_unit_status()` assumes unit names contain exactly one dot. Systemd device and mount unit names can legally contain multiple dots (e.g., `sys-devices-pci0000:00-<IPV6>.0.device`), causing the unpacking to fail.

**Fix:** Replace `split(".")` with `rsplit(".", 1)` which splits from the right at most once, correctly extracting the suffix (`.service`, `.device`, `.timer`, etc.) regardless of how many dots appear in the unit name.

**Verification:**
```python
# Old behavior (crashes):
>>> "sys-devices-pci0000:00-<IPV6>.0.device".split(".")
["sys-devices-pci0000:00-<IPV6>", "0", "device"]  # ValueError on unpack

# New behavior (works):
>>> "sys-devices-pci0000:00-<IPV6>.0.device".rsplit(".", 1)
["sys-devices-pci0000:00-<IPV6>.0", "device"]  # Correct
```

Normal service names (single dot) are unaffected:
```python
>>> "mock_bgp.service".rsplit(".", 1)
["mock_bgp", "service"]  # Same as before
```

## Test added
- `test_check_unit_status_multi_dot_unit_name`: verifies that `check_unit_status()` handles multi-dot unit names without crashing.

Fixes: #25291

There are many variables used to communicate between threads in eventd
(and its tests), and few of them have any synchronization (std::atomic
or explicit locking). This results in random test failures or crashes
when running the tests during a build. This could cause failures on real devices
but it's harder to find evidence of that.

To fix the lack of synchronization, I added std::atomic to all the
variables used to communicate between threads.

There was then the matter of the event_proxy. This sets up a proxy which
connects a couple of ZMQ sockets together. However, when tearing down
the sockets, the closing of the sockets was in the destructor which runs
on the main thread. We instead need to do all the interaction with the
zmq sockets owned by the proxy in the thread which the proxy runs. ZMQ
sockets are generally not allowed to be shared by different threads.
Re-arranged how the event proxy is started and quit in order to satisfy
the requirements of the ZMQ framework.

snappi_fixtures.py has function setup_dut_ports which has following sub-functions to select ports from snappi_ports:

Title: Bug: [ARP tests] CRM polling interval not set on all DUTs in multi-DUT testbeds Failure report: ### Is it platform specific generic ### Importance or Severity Medium ### Description of the bug The set_polling_interval fixture in tests/arp/conftest.py only sets CRM polling interval on a single DUT (duthost parameter). **Summary:**
Replace `time.sleep(300)` with `wait_until()` polling for Monit service readiness in `test_container_checker` and `test_container_checker_telemetry`.

**Context:** When the syncd container is stopped and needs recovery via `config_reload`, the test sleeps for a hardcoded 300 seconds (5 minutes) before proceeding. However, Monit initialization time varies depending on the platform and system load. If Monit takes longer than 300 seconds, the test proceeds before Monit is ready, causing it to miss alerting messages and fail. Conversely, when Monit initializes faster, the test wastes time sleeping.

**Fix:** Use `wait_until(360, 10, 30, check_monit_running, duthost)` which:
- Polls every 10 seconds for up to 360 seconds (6 min)
- Waits 30 seconds initially for config reload to settle
- Fails fast with a clear assertion if Monit never becomes ready
- Succeeds as soon as Monit is confirmed running (no wasted time)

This reuses the existing `check_monit_running()` helper already defined in the same test file and follows the `wait_until` pattern used throughout the codebase.

**Summary:**
This PR fixes excessive debug logging in `route_checker.py` that produces 10+ GB log files on T2 topologies, filling disks and slowing down test infrastructure.

**Context:** The `parse_routes_process()` and `parse_routes_process_vsonic()` functions call `eos_command()` and `shell()` with the default `verbose=True`. The Ansible debug logger then dumps both the full command arguments AND the complete results (thousands of BGP routing table entries per neighbor) into the log file. On T2 topologies with many VMs and large routing tables, this produces individual log files exceeding 10 GB.

**Fix:** Pass `verbose=False` to the `eos_command()` and `shell()` calls in the route parsing functions. This follows the existing pattern used by `parse_rib()` in `bgp_helpers.py` which already uses `verbose=False` for the same reason. Route data is parsed programmatically — there is no diagnostic value in logging the raw output. Errors are still properly reported via `pytest_assert`.

Fixes #19165

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
To prevent test log files from growing to 10+ GB, which fills disks and degrades test infrastructure on T2 topologies.

#### How did you do it?
Added `verbose=False` to three call sites in `tests/bgp/route_checker.py`:
1. `host.eos_command(commands=[cmd], module_ignore_errors=True, verbose=False)` — primary route query
2. `host.eos_command(commands=[cmd_backup], module_ignore_errors=True, verbose=False)` — fallback route query
3. `host.shell(bgp_nbr_cmd, verbose=False)` — vsonic route query

This matches the existing pattern in `parse_rib()` (`bgp_helpers.py:183`) which already uses `verbose=False`.

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Code review confirmed that `verbose=False` suppresses the DEBUG-level logging of command arguments and results in `AnsibleHostBase._run()` (`tests/common/devices/base.py:73-89, 119-128`)
- The `verbose=False` parameter is an established pattern already used in `parse_rib()` for the same reason
- Error handling via `pytest_assert` and `res['failed']` checks remains unchanged

#### Any platform specific information?

**Summary:**
Fix two bugs in `test_bgp_queue.py` that cause failures on IPv6-only topologies.

**Bug 1: NDP table footer parsed as valid entry**

The `show ndp` output ends with `Total number of entries N` which has exactly 5 space-separated fields. Since the parser only checks `len(items) != 5`, this footer line passes the filter and is parsed as:
- `ip = "Total"`
- `iface = "of"`

This pollutes `ndp_dict` with garbage entries. On IPv6-only topologies where all BGP neighbors use IPv6 addresses (resolved via NDP, not ARP), this causes either:
- Assertion failures when a valid IPv6 neighbor IP is not found in the polluted ndp_dict
- Queue counter checks against invalid interface name `"of"`

**Fix:** Add validation that the parsed IP field contains `:` (all IPv6 addresses do). Added similar validation for ARP entries (IP must start with a digit).

**Bug 2: Queue counters non-zero after single clear**

After `clear_queue_counters` + `time.sleep(10)`, BGP keepalive packets sent during the sleep window increment queue counters, leaving them non-zero when the assertion runs. On IPv6-only topologies with many BGP sessions (57 in the failing case), this is more likely.

**Fix:** Double-clear with short delays — clear, wait 5s (for keepalives), clear again, wait 5s. This ensures counters are zero when checked.

Fixes #20898

- [x] Bug fix

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
`test_bgp_queue.py` fails on IPv6-only topologies due to incorrect NDP table parsing and race condition with BGP keepalive traffic.

#### How did you do it?
1. Added IP format validation when parsing ARP/NDP tables to skip header/footer lines
2. Double-clear queue counters to handle BGP keepalive traffic between clear and check

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Root cause analysis from the traceback in #20898 shows `items = ["Total", "number", "of", "entries", "63"]` being parsed as a valid NDP entry
- The ARP table `"Total number of entries 4"` has 5 fields (not 4) so it was accidentally safe, but the NDP table footer has exactly 5 fields matching the filter
- The fix adds explicit IP format validation that cannot be confused with footer text

#### Any platform specific information?
Affects all platforms when running on IPv6-only topologies.

**Summary:**
This PR adds DUT-side validation of `show ip/ipv6 bgp neighbor advertised-routes` during TSA (Traffic Shift Away) to ensure only Loopback0 addresses are advertised.

Fixes #22364

### Type of change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
- [x] Test case improvement

### Back port request
- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The existing TSA tests verify that only loopback routes are received by neighbors (checking from the neighbor/EOS side using `received-routes`), but they do not verify from the DUT's own perspective. The DUT should also show only loopback prefixes in its `advertised-routes` output during TSA. This is a test gap identified in #22364.

#### How did you do it?
Added three new helper functions in `tests/bgp/route_checker.py`:

1. **`get_dut_advertised_routes(duthost, ip_ver)`** - Queries `show ip/ipv6 bgp neighbors <IP> advertised-routes json` on the DUT for each BGP neighbor from minigraph and returns a dict of `{peer_addr: set_of_prefixes}`.

2. **`verify_only_loopback_routes_in_dut_advertised_routes(dut_hosts, duthost, ip_ver)`** - Builds the expected loopback prefix set (same logic as existing `verify_loopback_route_with_community`) and compares it against the advertised prefixes for every neighbor.

3. **`assert_only_loopback_routes_in_dut_advertised_routes(dut_hosts, duthost, is_v6_topo)`** - `wait_until` wrapper (180s timeout, 10s interval) that asserts both IPv4 and IPv6 advertised-routes contain only loopback prefixes.

Added the new DUT-side check to three test functions in `test_traffic_shift.py`:
- `test_TSA`
- `test_TSA_TSB_with_config_reload`
- `test_load_minigraph_with_traffic_shift_away`

The new check runs after the existing neighbor-side verification, providing defense-in-depth: both the DUT and neighbor perspectives are validated.

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Code review confirmed the JSON output format of `show ip bgp neighbors <IP> advertised-routes json` returns `advertisedRoutes` dict with prefix keys and `totalPrefixCounter`
- The same JSON format is already used successfully in `test_bgp_azng_migration.py`
- Loopback prefix comparison logic mirrors the proven `verify_loopback_route_with_community()` function

#### Any platform specific information?
Generic - works on all platforms and topologies (t1, t2). Handles both IPv4-only and IPv6-only topologies.

#### Supported testbed topology if it is a new test case?
t1 (same as existing test_traffic_shift.py)

### Documentation
N/A

Title: Bug:Setting ring_thread_enabled to true in DEVICE_METADATA causes orchagent to fail during startup.

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

Setting ring_thread_enabled to true in DEVICE_METADATA causes orchagent to fail during startup. The failure is due to an invalid command-line invocation, where the -R option is passed without a required argument.

Set the following in config_db.json:
"ring_thread_enabled": "true"

Restart swss or reboot the device:
sudo systemctl restart swss
Observe that orchagent does not start.

/usr/bin/orchagent -d /var/log/swss -b 1024 -s \
  -m <IPV6> -q tcp://<IP> -R &
Observed Behavior
orchagent exits immediately with the following error:

/usr/bin/orchagent: option requires an argument -- 'R'
This indicates that the -R option is being passed without a required value.

### Steps to Reproduce

Set the following in config_db.json:
"ring_thread_enabled": "true"

Restart swss or reboot the device:
sudo systemctl restart swss
Observe that orchagent does not start.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

When ring_thread_enabled=true, orchagent should:

Start successfully, or

Validate required parameters and fall back safely if missing.

-R must not be passed without its mandatory argument.

### Relevant log output

```shell
/usr/bin/orchagent -d /var/log/swss -b 1024 -s -m <IPV6> -q tcp://<IP> -R &
[1] 276
root@ixr-x1b-2:/# /usr/bin/orchagent: option requires an argument -- 'R'

[1]+  Exit 1                  /usr/bin/orchagent -d /var/log/swss -b 1024 -s -m <IPV6> -q tcp://<IP> -R
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell
SONiC Software Version: SONiC.nokia-master.0-dirty-20260202.102116
SONiC OS Version: 13
Distribution: Debian 13.3
Kernel: 6.12.41+deb13-sonic-arm64
Build commit: cfc90a838
Build date: Mon Feb  2 <IPV6> UTC 2026
```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

Retrieved SONiC documentation:

[1] error-handling/orchagent_error_handling.md — Warmboot and Fastboot Design Impact (score=200.628)
This error handling improvement does not have any requirements or dependencies w.r.t warmboot or fastboot.
In the going down path, warm reboot does not currently go through when there are pending orchagent entries that have yet to be programmed to ASIC_DB and that behavior will stay as-is. In the going up path after SWSS state restoration, there should be no pending entries in m_toSync map.

[2] multi_asic/SONiC_multi_asic_hld.md — 2.4.2.3. ASIC initialization (score=196.278)
When orchagent initializes it fills in the SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_SWITCH_HARDWARE_INFO with the ASIC_ID and calls SAI create switch.
The SAI should parse the ASIC ID and initialize the ASIC with a specific device identifier.

The PCI device ID, stored in the asic.conf, is used as the ASIC_ID.  

***orchagent.sh*** has been updated to take a new option ***-i*** to pass the ASIC_ID as argument to orchagent.

The ASIC host-interface(knet) driver links the ports to namespace, where the swss/syncd is running for that ASIC instance, in the kernel.

[3] warm-reboot/open_issues.md — What are the major steps to perform docker warm upgrade? (score=194.026)
r image,   docker image path.

Ex.
```
      sonic-installer upgrade_docker --cleanup_image swss swss_test_02 ./docker-orchagent-brcm_test_02.gz
```

More options are to be provided like whether to enforce stringent state check and validation.

3. Docker warm restart

For simple docker warm restart,  after the config step, just use systemd command.
Ex.
```
  systemctl restart swss
```

**What I did**
Fixed a typo in the getopt option string in `orchagent/main.cpp` where the `-R` option was incorrectly defined as requiring a mandatory argument (`R:`) instead of being a simple flag (`R`).

The fix changes line 403 from:
```cpp
while ((opt = getopt(argc, argv, "b:m:r:f:j:d:i:hsz:k:q:c:t:v:I:R:D:M")) != -1)
```
to:
```cpp
while ((opt = getopt(argc, argv, "b:m:r:f:j:d:i:hsz:k:q:c:t:v:I:RD:M")) != -1)
```

**Why I did it**

When ring_thread_enabled is set to true in DEVICE_METADATA, orchagent fails to start with the error:
`/usr/bin/orchagent: option requires an argument -- 'R'`

This bug was introduced in PR #3814 (specifically, commit 5de59222) when the -D option was added.

The getopt string was changed from `I:R` to `I:R:D:` instead of the correct `I:RD:`.

This accidentally added a colon after R, making it require a mandatory argument.

**How I verified it**

I did a code review and verified that the -R case handler does not use `optarg` and simply sets `gRingMode = true`. Also, I have checked the git history and traced the bug introduction to PR #3814 and confirmed the original implementation in PR #3242 was correct.

Check the code lines here:

Original PR link:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/pull/3242/changes#diff-3cba33a216c0ea2b942dc03b2638fa27a40a8b6eb81abf9f83f13e1ee7831ac4R360

Bug Link:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/pull/3814/changes#diff-3cba33a216c0ea2b942dc03b2638fa27a40a8b6eb81abf9f83f13e1ee7831ac4R373

**Details if related**

Title: Bug: [orchagent] SIGSEGV in AclRange::remove due to infinite loop in error-handling path

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific
yes

### Importance or Severity
Critical

### Description of the bug

A SIGSEGV occurs in orchagent within the AclRange::remove function. The crash is caused by a logic error in a for loop where the loop boundary variable is incremented instead of the iterator, leading to an infinite loop and eventual out-of-bounds memory access.

**To Reproduce**

1. Attempt to create an ACL rule (e.g., EVERFLOW) on a platform where the specific attribute combination is not supported by the SAI (returning SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED).

2. The AclRule::createRule fails and enters the cleanup path.

3. AclRange::remove is called to clean up range objects.

4. The process crashes immediately.

**Expected behavior**: The AclRange::remove function should iterate through the range OIDs exactly once, perform the cleanup, and allow orchagent to log the SAI error and continue running.

**Actual behavior**: The process terminates with signal SIGSEGV.

**Log portions**:
`ERR swss#orchagent: :- createRule: Failed to create ACL rule RULE_1, rv:-2`
`ERR swss#orchagent: :- create: create status: SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`
`INFO swss#supervisord 2026-01-21 <IPV6>,462 WARN exited: orchagent (terminated by SIGSEGV (core dumped); not expected) `

1. Return `task_success` --  No crash, no retry, handled successfully.

The failure handling function should return `task_success` when the failure is properly handled without the need for another attempt (e.g., the SAI status is `SAI_STATUS_ITEM_NOT_FOUND` in remove operation).

2. Return `task_failed` -- No crash, no retry, although the failure is not handled successfully, orchagent will keep running without exit.

The failure handling function should return `task_failed` when the failure is unable to be handled in orchagent and another attempt is not likely to resolve the failure. In suc...

g ACL, conflicting IP addresses), hardware permanent error, non-critical internal logic error, etc.

3. Return `task_need_retry` --  No crash, retry

The failure handling function should return `task_need_retry` when the failed SAI call may be resolved in a subsequent attempt.

4. exit(EXIT_FAILURE) -- Crash and trigger SwSS auto-restart

Some of the failures can be resolved by restarting SwSS.
In the scenario where such failures happen, the failure handling function in the orchagent should exit with `EXIT_FAILURE` and trigger SwSS auto restart.

one of three actions will be performed in one of the handleSai<Op>Status() functions in orchagent, depending on whether the operation was a create, set, remove or get:

 a. If the error is something that can resolve itself with subsequent retries like for eg: SAI_STATUS_OBJECT_IN_USE or SAI_STATUS_TABLE_FULL, handleSai<Op>Status() will return task_need_retry. In this case, the entry is not removed from the m_toSync map. No errors are logged in such...

This patch is to fix a major bug in the for loop of the function AclRange::remove.

**What I did**
Fixed a critical logic error in AclRange::remove where the loop limit (oidsCnt) was being incremented instead of the loop index (oidIdx).

**Why I did it**
The original code contained an infinite loop: for (int oidIdx = 0; oidIdx < oidsCnt; oidsCnt++). This caused Memory Corruption/Crash: The loop would continue until oidsCnt accessed memory outside the bounds of the oids pointer, resulting in a SIGSEGV (Segmentation Fault).

**How I verified it**
After the fix, orchagent remains stable and correctly logs the SAI error (rv:-2) instead of terminating.

**Details if related**
The crash was specifically observed in Arista Gardena switches.

Fixes: [sonic-qual.msft](https://github.com/aristanetworks/sonic-qual.msft/issues/1067)

## What I did
Add SIGINT and SIGTERM trap handlers to `scripts/process_log.sh` so that pressing Ctrl-C during a build actually terminates the build.

## Why I did it
Currently, pressing Ctrl-C during a SONiC build (especially during the trixie phase) does not reliably abort the build. The build appears to hang or continue running in the background.

**Root cause:** The `LOG` macro in `rules/functions` pipes all build output through `process_log.sh`:

```makefile
LOG = < /dev/null |& $(PROJECT_ROOT)/scripts/process_log.sh -t &>> $(PROJECT_ROOT)/$@.log
```

When the user presses Ctrl-C:
1. The terminal sends SIGINT to the foreground process group
2. `make` receives it and tries to kill child processes
3. But `process_log.sh` 's `while IFS= read -r line` loop **does not exit on SIGINT** — bash's `read` builtin is not reliably interruptible by signals
4. This keeps the pipe open, preventing the upstream build command from being cleaned up
5. The build appears stuck or continues in the background

Fixes: #25520

## How I did it
Added two trap handlers at the top of `process_log.sh`:
```bash
trap 'exit 130' INT    # 128 + 2 (SIGINT)
trap 'exit 143' TERM   # 128 + 15 (SIGTERM)
```

These ensure the script exits immediately when signaled, allowing the pipeline to tear down and make to clean up properly.

## How I verified it
1. Started a VS build with `make SONIC_BUILD_JOBS=4 target/sonic-vs.img.gz`
2. Pressed Ctrl-C during package compilation phase
3. Verified build processes terminate within seconds (previously would hang)
4. Verified normal build operation is unaffected — process_log.sh still correctly timestamps and forwards all output when not interrupted

Title: Enhancement: [sflow] wait_for conditions rather than use sleep() for test orchestration

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

sflow/test_sflow.py currently makes liberal use of `sleep()` calls to ensure timing coordination between the various components of the sflow path. This is very brittle; timing changes in unrelated code paths can cause these coordination pauses to become insufficient, and conversely improvements in timing would lead to lots of wasted time waiting for nothing. Further, the timing might be different depending on the device. To make this a more general test, we should identify what the actual conditions are that need to be satisfied at each stage and add explicit `wait_for()` logic in those places.

### Current Behavior

The test uses `sleep()` in the main test as well as in the PTF script to ensure that everything has been set up correctly before traffic is sent.

### Proposed Behavior

The test uses `wait_for()` with an appropriate condition instead.

#### Why I did it

Fixes #20614.

`asic_sensors_config.py` and `smartswitch_config.py` call `device_info.get_path_to_platform_dir()` without handling the `OSError` raised when no platform directory exists. This causes `test_minigraph_packet_chassis_acl_local_host` (and several related tests) to fail during the `sonic_config_engine` wheel build, breaking the entire image build.

Multiple users have reported this across different platforms (Marvell AMD64, VS ARM64, VS x86_64) — see #20614.

#### Root Cause Analysis

The failure chain:

1. `test_minigraph_packet_chassis_acl_local_host` sets `CFGGEN_UNIT_TESTING = ""` (clearing it to avoid stale mock port data from previous tests that would break yang validation)
2. `run_script()` → `YangWrapper.validate()` spawns a **subprocess**: `sonic-cfggen -m <graph> --print-data`
3. The subprocess inherits `CFGGEN_UNIT_TESTING=""`. Since it is not `"2"`, `mock_tables.dbconnector` is **not** loaded
4. `sonic-cfggen` → `main()` → calls `get_asic_sensors_config()`
5. `get_asic_sensors_config()` checks `CFGGEN_UNIT_TESTING == "2"` → false, takes the `else` branch
6. Calls `device_info.get_path_to_platform_dir()` **directly with no guard**
7. Inside the build container: no `PLATFORM` env var, no `/host/machine.conf`, no `/usr/share/sonic/platform` directory → **`OSError("Failed to locate platform directory")`**

```
Traceback:
  sonic-cfggen:404  main()        → parse_xml(minigraph, platform, ...)
  minigraph.py:2064 parse_xml()   → get_port_config(hwsku=hwsku, ...)
  portconfig.py:193               → device_info.get_path_to_port_config_file(hwsku, asic_id)
  device_info.py:443              → get_path_to_platform_dir()
  device_info.py:264              → raise OSError("Failed to locate platform directory")
```

The same pattern exists in `smartswitch_config.py`. Additionally, `smartswitch_config.py` has a secondary bug: when `CFGGEN_UNIT_TESTING == "2"` but the hwsku does not match either known test value (`SSwitch-32x1000Gb` or `SS-DPU-1x400Gb`), `json_file` is never assigned, causing an `UnboundLocalError`.

#### How I did it

- **`asic_sensors_config.py`**: Wrap the `get_path_to_platform_dir()` call in a `try/except OSError` block. When no platform directory exists, return an empty config dict (no ASIC sensor data is available, which is the correct behavior for non-device environments).

- **`smartswitch_config.py`**: Same `try/except OSError` guard, plus add an `else` clause for unrecognized hwsku values during unit testing to return empty config instead of hitting `UnboundLocalError`.

This is consistent with the existing pattern in `device_info.get_path_to_port_config_file()`, which safely checks `get_platform()` before attempting to locate the platform directory:

```python
platform = get_platform()
if not platform:
    return None
```

#### How to verify it

**Reproduce the failure (before fix):**

```bash

make configure PLATFORM=vs
make target/python-wheels/bookworm/sonic_config_engine-1.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

Look for:
```
FAILED tests/test_cfggen.py::TestCfgGen::test_minigraph_packet_chassis_acl_local_host
  OSError: Failed to locate platform directory
```

**After fix:** The above build step should pass with 0 test failures.

The fix is also safe on real devices: when a platform directory exists, `get_path_to_platform_dir()` succeeds and behavior is unchanged. The `try/except` only catches the `OSError` for environments where no platform is configured.

#### Description for the changelog

Guard `get_path_to_platform_dir()` calls in `asic_sensors_config.py` and `smartswitch_config.py` to handle missing platform directories gracefully, fixing build failures in non-device environments.

## Description

When a management interface uses a /31 or /32 subnet (RFC 3021 point-to-point links), `netaddr.IPNetwork.broadcast` returns `None`. The `prefix_attr()` function in `sonic-cfggen` converts this to the string `"None"` via `str()`, which then renders literally as `broadcast None` in `/etc/network/interfaces`.

This causes ifupdown to emit warnings and breaks network configuration:
```
warning: eth0: convert string ip address into IPNetwork object:
'None' does not appear to be an IPv4 or IPv6 address
```

**Affected subnets:**
- IPv4: /31, /32
- IPv6: /127, /128

### Fix

Two changes (defense in depth):

1. **`sonic-cfggen` `prefix_attr()`**: Check for `None` before calling `str()`, returning `None` instead of the string `"None"`.

2. **`interfaces.j2`**: Guard the broadcast line with `{% if prefix | broadcast %}` so it is omitted when the broadcast address is `None`.

### Before (broken)
```
iface eth0 inet static
    address <IP>
    netmask <IP>
    network <IP>
    broadcast None     ← invalid
```

### After (fixed)
```
iface eth0 inet static
    address <IP>
    netmask <IP>
    network <IP>
                       ← broadcast line correctly omitted
```

Normal subnets (/24, /64, etc.) are unaffected — broadcast line still renders as before.

## Test added
- New minigraph test data (`t0-sample-graph-mgmt31.xml`) with /31 mgmt interface
- Expected output (`interfaces_mgmt31`) verifying broadcast line is omitted for /31
- Test case in `test_j2files.py::test_interfaces`

Fixes: #25150

Title: Bug: everflow test fails with 'Port mirror direction both is not supported by the ASIC'

Failure report:
## Description

The everflow test `test_everflow_basic_forwarding` fails during mirror session setup because the ASIC does not support bidirectional port mirroring.

## Error

```
config mirror_session add test_session_1 <IP> <IP> 8 4 35006

Error: Port mirror direction 'both' is not supported by the ASIC
```

## Failing Test

```
everflow/test_everflow_testbed.py::TestEverflowV4IngressAclIngressMirror::test_everflow_basic_forwarding[erspan_ipv4-cli-downstream-default]
```

## Root Cause Analysis

This is caused by a bug in **sonic-utilities PR [#4089](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4089)** (merged Nov 17, 2025), which added mirror capability checking but introduced a regression:

### What PR #4089 did:
1. Added `is_port_mirror_capability_supported(direction)` to check `PORT_INGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE` / `PORT_EGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE` in STATE_DB before allowing mirror session creation.
2. Added the `direction` parameter to `config mirror_session erspan add` and `config mirror_session span add` subcommands.
3. **Missed adding `direction` to the legacy `config mirror_session add` command** (line ~2976 in config/main.py).

### How the failure occurs:
1. The test calls `config mirror_session add` (legacy command, no `direction` parameter).
2. Legacy `add` calls `add_erspan(direction=None)`.
3. `validate_mirror_session_config(direction=None)` calls `is_port_mirror_capability_supported(None)`.
4. With `direction=None`, it checks **both** `PORT_INGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE` and `PORT_EGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE`.
5. On platforms where orchagent does not populate these STATE_DB keys, `state_db.get()` returns `None`, and `None != "true"` causes the check to fail.
6. CLI rejects the session with: `Error: Port mirror direction 'both' is not supported by the ASIC`.

### Key insight:
The legacy `config mirror_session add` command never used directional mirroring. Before PR #4089, it worked fine on all platforms. The capability check should either:
- Not apply when `direction` is `None` and `src_port` is `None` (legacy ERSPAN path), or
- The legacy command should accept a `direction` parameter like the `erspan add` subcommand does.

### CLI behavior comparison:
| Command | direction param | Capability check | Result on affected platforms |
|---------|----------------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| `config mirror_session add` (legacy) | NOT supported | Checks both (direction=None) | **FAILS** |
| `config mirror_session erspan add` | Positional arg | Checks specified direction | Works if direction matches capability |
| `config mirror_session span add` | Positional arg | Checks specified direction | Works if direction matches capability |

## Fix

### sonic-utilities (root cause):
Filed as **sonic-net/sonic-utilities#4318** - Legacy `config mirror_session add` missing direction parameter after PR #4089.

### sonic-mgmt (test-side workaround):
PR **#22663** adds:
1. **Capability pre-check**: Skip tests when ASIC doesn't report mirror capabilities in STATE_DB (defaults to `"false"` when absent, matching CLI behavior).
2. **CLI fallback**: Try legacy `config mirror_session add` first; if it fails, retry with `config mirror_session erspan add` (which accepts direction); if both fail, skip with image mismatch message.
3. **Unified IPv4/IPv6 path**: Both use the same CLI fallback instead of IPv6 writing directly to CONFIG_DB.

## Environment

Observed in Azure Pipeline PR checker CI (PR #22657). Affects all images built after sonic-utilities PR #4089 was merged (Nov 17, 2025).

*This issue was filed by an AI agent on behalf of @yxieca.*

## What is the motivation for this PR?

The everflow tests fail on ASICs that do not support bidirectional port mirroring. When `config mirror_session add` is called without an explicit `--direction` flag, SONiC defaults to `both`, which requires both `PORT_INGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE` and `PORT_EGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE` to be `true` in `STATE_DB SWITCH_CAPABILITY|switch`. On ASICs that don't support both directions, the command fails with:
```
Error: Port mirror direction 'both' is not supported by the ASIC
```
This causes test failures unrelated to the test logic itself.

Fixes #22661

## How did you do it?

Added a capability check in the `setup_mirror_session` and `policer_mirror_session` fixtures in `everflow_test_utilities.py`. Before attempting to create a mirror session via CLI, the fixtures now query `switch_capabilities_facts` for `PORT_INGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE` and `PORT_EGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE`. If either capability is not `true`, the test is skipped with a descriptive message.

The check is only applied for `CONFIG_MODE_CLI` since the direct DB write path (used for IPv6 ERSPAN) bypasses the CLI validation.

## How did you verify/test it?

- Code review of SONiC's `config/main.py` confirms `is_port_mirror_capability_supported()` checks these exact fields when direction is `None` (defaults to 'both')
- The skip message includes actual capability values for debugging
- Existing tests on platforms that support bidirectional mirroring are unaffected (capabilities default to `true` when not present in STATE_DB)

## What I did

Fixed is_port_mirror_capability_supported() so that ERSPAN sessions (direction=None) are not blocked by the PORT_INGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE / PORT_EGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE capability check.

## Root cause

PR #4089 added a capability check that reads PORT_INGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE and PORT_EGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE from STATE_DB SWITCH_CAPABILITY|switch. For ERSPAN sessions, direction=None was treated as 'check both', but:
1. These capability flags only apply to SPAN (port mirror) sessions, not ERSPAN (which uses source/destination IPs, not ports)
2. Platforms that don't populate these STATE_DB keys return None, which != 'true', so the function incorrectly returns False (unsupported)

PR #4159 partially addressed the multi-ASIC namespace issue but did not fix the fundamental problem for ERSPAN sessions with no src/dst port specified.

## How I fixed it

- **For ERSPAN (direction=None)**: Return True immediately. PORT_INGRESS/EGRESS_MIRROR_CAPABLE does not apply to ERSPAN sessions.
- **For SPAN (direction != None)**: Treat absent STATE_DB key (None value) as 'supported' for backward compatibility with platforms that don't populate SWITCH_CAPABILITY table entries.

Unit tests updated in 	ests/config_mirror_session_test.py:
- Added Test 4 to verify behavior when STATE_DB keys are absent (all return True)
- Updated Test 2 and Test 3 assertions for direction=None to expect True

Title: 'show version' crashes in docker-sonic-vs: missing debian_version and kernel_version in sonic_version.yml

Failure report:
## Description
`show version` crashes with `KeyError: 'debian_version'` inside docker-sonic-vs containers because `sonic_version.yml` does not include `debian_version` or `kernel_version` fields.

## Root Cause
`sonic_version.yml.j2` conditionally includes `debian_version` and `kernel_version` only when those variables are defined during the build:

```jinja2
{% if debian_version is defined -%}
debian_version: '{{ debian_version }}'
{% endif -%}

For docker-sonic-vs, these variables are not set during the docker build, so the fields are omitted from the generated `sonic_version.yml`.

Fixed intermittent build failure in `ctrmgr_iptables_test.py::TestIPTableUpdate::test_table` (#23432).

#### How I did it
1. **Mocked `socket.gethostbyname`** — the test was calling real DNS resolution which is environment-dependent. On build machines with DNS hijacking or NXDOMAIN redirection (common in corporate/Azure environments), invalid hostnames like `www.google.comx` resolve to a proxy IP instead of failing, causing unexpected test results.

2. **Replaced `www.google.comx` with `host.invalid`** — the `.invalid` TLD is reserved by [RFC 6761](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6761) and guaranteed to never resolve, providing an extra safety net.

3. **Added explicit `ret` assertion to test case 3** — previously test case 3 (`www.google.com`) only checked `post_rules` via regex `.*` but never verified the return value. Now it asserts the deterministic mock IP.

Test case 4 passes `ip="www.google.comx"` expecting `_get_ip()` → `socket.gethostbyname()` to fail (return `""`). Title: Bug:[202511/Trixie] pmon container init fails when IMAGE_VERSION is unset (container_startup.py gets empty -v)

Failure report:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

On 202511/Trixie, the pmon container’s docker_init.sh (from docker-platform-monitor/docker_init.j2) always calls container_startup.py with -v ${IMAGE_VERSION}. When IMAGE_VERSION is not set, this expands to a bare -v and argparse aborts (expected one argument), causing PMON startup/health checks to fail. Setting a default version (e.g., ${IMAGE_VERSION:-0.0.0}) prevents the crash and allows PMON to start normally.

### Steps to Reproduce

Boot a SONiC 202511 / Trixie image on a DUT.

Ensure IMAGE_VERSION is not set in the pmon container init environment (this happens by default in the failing cases).

Restart PMON (or trigger any action that restarts it), for example:

sudo systemctl restart pmon.service
(alternatively: run config load_minigraph -y, which often restarts containers as part of config reload)

Observe pmon startup failure logs:

container_startup.py: error: argument -v/--version: expected one argument

followed by pmon being marked unhealthy / critical service check reporting pmon: False.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual Behavior:
On 202511/Trixie, pmon startup can fail because docker_init.sh invokes container_startup.py with -v ${IMAGE_VERSION} and when IMAGE_VERSION is unset it expands to a bare -v, causing argparse to error (expected one argument). This leads to PMON failing to initialize properly and health/critical-service checks reporting pmon as down/unhealthy.

Expected Behavior:
pmon should start reliably even when IMAGE_VERSION is not set; container_startup.py should receive a valid version string (or a safe default) and proceed without argument parsing errors, keeping PMON healthy and critical-service checks passing.

### Relevant log output

### Description of PR

Summary:
Fix IMAGE_VERSION being empty in all multi-stage Docker container builds.

In Docker multi-stage builds, `ARG` values **do not carry over between stages** — each `FROM` resets the ARG scope. All 15 container Dockerfiles that use `rsync_from_builder_stage()` declare `ARG image_version` in the builder stage but not in the final stage. The `ENV IMAGE_VERSION=$image_version` in the final stage therefore resolves to an empty string.

When `container_startup.py` is invoked with `-v ${IMAGE_VERSION}` and `IMAGE_VERSION` is empty, argparse fails with:
```
container_startup.py: error: argument -v/--version: expected one argument
```

This causes the container init to abort, leading to container health check failures.

**Root cause:** Missing `ARG image_version` in the final build stage of multi-stage Dockerfiles.

**Fix:** Add `ARG image_version` after the final `FROM $BASE` in all 15 affected Dockerfile.j2 files:
- docker-bmp-watchdog
- docker-dhcp-relay
- docker-dhcp-server
- docker-eventd
- docker-gnmi-sidecar
- docker-lldp
- docker-platform-monitor (pmon)
- docker-router-advertiser
- docker-snmp
- docker-sonic-bmp
- docker-sonic-gnmi
- docker-sonic-otel
- docker-sonic-telemetry
- docker-telemetry-sidecar
- docker-telemetry-watchdog

Fixes #25683

Supersedes #25684 (which only added a `:-0.0.0` default to pmon's docker_init.j2 — a symptom-level fix for one container)

#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Container init scripts fail when `IMAGE_VERSION` is unset because `container_startup.py -v` receives no argument.

#### How did you do it?
Added `ARG image_version` in the final build stage of each affected Dockerfile.j2, right after `FROM $BASE`. This ensures the Docker build-arg `image_version` is available when `ENV IMAGE_VERSION=$image_version` is evaluated in the final stage.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Verified that the Dockerfile pattern matches the Docker multi-stage build ARG scoping rules per [Docker documentation](https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#understand-how-arg-and-from-interact).

Example — before (broken):
```dockerfile
FROM $BASE AS base
ARG image_version            # scoped to 'base' stage only

{{ rsync_from_builder_stage() }}
ENV IMAGE_VERSION=$image_version  # $image_version is EMPTY
```

```dockerfile
FROM $BASE AS base
ARG image_version
ENV IMAGE_VERSION=$image_version
...
FROM $BASE
ARG image_version            # re-declared in final stage
{{ rsync_from_builder_stage() }}
ENV IMAGE_VERSION=$image_version  # now resolves correctly
```
